thesis: A confirmed swing-high breakout is the point at which the resting supply that had capped a stock at its last significant pivot has been absorbed; the marginal buyer transacting above that level does so with less overhead resistance than existed a session earlier, and the marginal seller who anchored to the old high as fair value is now underwater and stepping aside rather than defending a broken level. The 200-day trend filter restricts entries to names whose broader supply/demand balance already favors buyers, so a breakout is read as continuation of an existing imbalance rather than a reversal bet on a name that has been going nowhere. The counterparty on the other side of a fill is not a rational price-setter reacting to the breakout itself: it is a momentum-agnostic seller (an index-fund rebalancer, a tax-loss seller, an investor rotating out of the name for reasons unrelated to its chart) or a trend-following short who is stopped out as the level gives way. Neither is pricing the breakout; that mispricing is the edge being harvested, and it should decay if enough capital chases the same signal. This card spreads that one mechanism across six economically distinct sectors -- semiconductors, e-commerce/big-box retail, heavy industrial equipment, energy services, money-center banking, and managed care/pharma -- specifically so a result speaks to the mechanism rather than to one sector's beta, which a single-sector or single-asset-class breakout card cannot separate.
entry: close crosses_above swing_high(20) and close > sma(200)
